title: Returns the wrong 'best mark'
plain: A new function finds a student's best mark, but it skips the very first mark in the list. If their best mark happened to be first, it reports the wrong number. No crash - just a silently wrong answer, which is worse.
diff:
--- a/marks.py
+++ b/marks.py
@@ -26,6 +26,16 @@
     return max(student["marks"])
 
 
+def best_mark(student_id):
+    """Return the student's best mark."""
+    student = find_student(student_id)
+    best = 0
+    for mark in student["marks"][1:]:
+        if mark > best:
+            best = mark
+    return best
+
+
 def has_passed(student_id):
     """A student passes if their average is 40 or more."""
     return average_marks(student_id) >= 40
